section.title: Removing whole URLs
section.para: The package opennlp.tools.normalizer.url provides BoundedUrlCharSequenceNormalizer, a CharSequenceNormalizer that replaces each HTTP or HTTPS URL and each email address with one space. A URL runs to the next Unicode whitespace, control character, typographic quotation mark, or one of < > ", so ports, user information, percent escapes, bracketed IPv6 hosts, and non-ASCII host names and paths are removed with it. Trailing sentence punctuation, a trailing apostrophe and closing brackets without an opening bracket in the URL are kept. A scheme must start the text or follow a character other than a letter, digit, underscore, plus, hyphen, period, or colon, so git+https:// and see:http:// are not HTTP URLs. URLs with other schemes are kept, and no email address is matched inside them. The normalizer is stateless and safe for concurrent use.

section.title: Using it for language detection
section.para: Since 3.0.0 core's UrlCharSequenceNormalizer removes whole URLs the same way, and under CompatibilityMode.LEGACY it produces the ASCII-bounded output the language detector models before 3.0.0 were trained with. This normalizer has no compatibility mode. To use it, supply a custom LanguageDetectorFactory whose getContextGenerator() uses it, and use that factory for both training and inference. A model trained with one URL normalizer must be decoded with the same one, and changing it requires evaluation.
The normalizer finds URL boundaries in running text. It does not validate URLs against the WHATWG URL Standard.
